items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: No, John never worked in the record department.

ctx.x: But you mean like John Reed?

No, John never worked in the record department. He met some of the engineers, that would be in the 1950s. But anyway, recording is nothing to brag about. But I decided then to issue some of the things myself. In 1945, I decided to go into the business myself and issue them. So I began getting impressed. That was during the war wasn't over yet, even. items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I also have a couple of pages of information on George Bach K., which I obtained from John Reed about 1943.

ctx.x: This is an interview with Bill Russell at Seminar Room 2 in the Harvard Tilton Memorial Library at Tulane University. This is Rio 1, the date is September 4th, 1962.

We'd been talking about some of the, this is Bill Russell again, some of the musicians that I'd interviewed at various times preparing for the book Jazz Man, and other times after that, that we weren't able to talk to because most of them are dead now. We weren't able to interview them for our Jazz Archive directly here. One of them was George Bach K., whom I stopped to see in Philadelphia in 1940, fall of 1940.
